title: Victory does not come with a roof
notes: P5.01 is War Pictorial News 213 (British MOI newsreel, 4 June 1945): VE Day faces in a packed London crowd, Union Jacks and a placard. The plan's 111-adc-4267 London segment IS Piccadilly Circus (shot 76, 576.48-582.48: the Criterion building's canopy with its name, flags and bunting, a queue and crowd below), but it is US Army Signal Corps footage and no fitting label is rendered (the cards have AMERICAN FOOTAGE · 1937 and AMERICAN FILM · 1944, neither true of it), so it is held as the alternate: swap in 576.7-581.7 once a LABEL-AMERICAN-FOOTAGE-1945 exists.
111-M-1211 (The True Glory): its last reels are the Reims/Berlin surrender and war graves, nothing of the London celebration; not used.
P5.03 Battersea girls (HU49414, 5335 px) pushed toward the rubble at their feet.

P5.04: 'Debt is enormous' on What A Life!'s office piled with forms; 'Supplies are short' on its wide bus queue (shot 11; scene 03 uses the next shot, 12, the close faces of the same queue, at 179.0); 'Rationing continues' on Pop Goes the Weasel's 1948 grocer's counter (National Butter, prices on cards). LABEL-1949-COMEDY covers only the two What A Life! clips.

P5.05 is Diary for Timothy's prefab going up (1945: men lifting wall panels on to a frame, a row of finished prefabs behind), civilian production released from war. The plan's miner sequence is at 12:18-12:31 in this file (#79-80, not 17:00-30:00) and was not needed.
P5.06 'Taxes and borrowing' on Pop Goes the Weasel's hand writing PEACE AND WAR across an envelope (the 1948 Treasury film).

P5.07 imports: War Pictorial News 213 has no docks or shipping on its sheets (Food to Holland, Germany, the surrender, London crowds), and NARA-531280 is a VE Day hug, not imports, so this uses Know Your Ally's dock shots (crates slung ashore, a Ford crate), labelled AMERICAN FILM · 1944 on V4. They show wartime US imports to Britain under a 1945 line; the label keeps it honest.
P5.08 the loan-signing photograph is the right year here (Washington, 6 Dec 1945; Keynes seated far left). INSET, 799 px.

P5.10 is the 1946 Victory Parade (Universal Newsreel) march past the royal dais, as the plan asks; P5.11-12 ('Debt is a burden. It isn't a veto.') cut to Pop Goes the Weasel's builders on a roof and scaffold (1948), so the line about rebuilding lands on rebuilding. Scene 10 uses the next shot of that sequence (bricklayers, 421.55).
No credit string exists in footage.md for War Pictorial News 213, the Victory Parade reel or Know Your Ally; left null.
orchestrator: added LABEL-AMERICAN-NEWSREEL-1946 over 07-16 (the Victory Parade reel is American).
